desk.headline: Revenue up 17% to a record Q3 $2.3bn; 2026 revenue and cash flow outlook raised

other.label: Net cash (ex Eve)
other.change: vs net debt of $214.5m in Q2

results: Revenue grew 17% to $2.3bn, a third-quarter record, with every unit up: services +30%, defense +22%, commercial jets +13% and business jets +12%.
The adjusted EBIT margin rose to 10.9% from 8.6%, helped by better prices and mix and no US import tariffs this quarter.
Net income fell to $71.1m ($0.40 per ADS) from $116.6m on higher finance costs and taxes.
Adjusted free cash flow (ex Eve) was $627.7m, driven by customer deposits, turning the balance sheet to net cash of $430m.
The backlog hit a record $35.7bn; defense orders were up 56% from a year ago.

guidance.summary: Embraer raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $8.4–8.6bn and its free cash flow target to at least $700m. The margin and delivery ranges stayed the same.

points: The finance chief tied the higher outlook to strong performance across the business.
Supply shortages were about 25% lower than in 2025, but engines and some parts like windshields still disrupt output.
Q4 will carry many commercial jet deliveries at below-average margins, plus yearly defense contract price adjustments.
Q4 cash will be used to build stock for 2027 deliveries; over time free cash flow should be about half of EBITDA, with 2027 likely lower.
Eve, the electric air taxi unit, is spending about $50–55m a quarter, with crewed prototype flights planned for the second half of 2027.
call.source: Call transcript — The Motley Fool, 10 Nov 2026

watch: Whether the heavy Q4 delivery schedule is met despite engine supply limits.
Q4 margins as lower-margin commercial jets dominate deliveries.
The ADS ratio change from four shares to one on 16 Nov 2026, which changes per-ADS figures.
